analysis:
Only docs/architecture/inference.md changed (date bump; GLM video paragraph near base lines 810-813 and 827; additions at head 876-895 and 1732-1751). The supplied patch excerpt is truncated, so the head 876-895 and 1732-1751 additions were not visible. I reviewed the base text of units 4 and 5 and the visible patch hunks.

Visible change: the documentation now says GLM5Next video indexes variable-frame-rate tracks instead of refusing them. Frame i is timed at i / nominalFrameRate, matching the reference loader. Variable-frame-rate refusals are removed from the deterministic-400 list.

Security relevance: this is a documented behavioral change in the provider's video decode path. Related threats are TB-007 and TB-003 (inline media plaintext, T-050) and DoS through resource exhaustion (T-010/T-029). The documented bounds are unchanged: 512 MiB decoded-frame cap, 2 FPS sampling, 28,532 visual-token cap, VisionMemoryGate reservation, and media excluded from prefix cache. A VFR track might read many more frames, but frames are read one at a time and only 2 FPS samples are kept within the cap. The patch is documentation only, and the docs claim these bounds still apply. I cannot verify the Swift implementation (GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset) from the supplied evidence, and I cannot confirm that frame-by-frame reading of a VFR track is bounded in CPU or time.

I found no concrete regression in the visible text and no threat-model contradiction. The prefix-cache text (T-041) is unchanged context. The next pass should check the source change behind the doc edit: a bounded frame-read count, no temp-file plaintext for the video (T-050), and a timestamp-computation overflow guard on nominalFrameRate=0.
